issue.title: ACP tool-result handling crashes on FunctionToolResultEvent.result

steps:
Create a file named notes.txt in the current directory containing exactly one line: release-code=ALPHA-7731
Reply with the word done once the file has been written.
What release code did I ask you to put into notes.txt in my previous message? Please answer from our conversation.
expected: After a tool executes, stream its result to the ACP client and continue the task to a final answer. A successful file write must not be followed by an adapter AttributeError disguised as an ordinary end_turn.
defect: The ACP adapter accesses FunctionToolResultEvent.result after the tool has already executed. With the recorded dependency version, this attribute does not exist. The turn stops with an AttributeError message and end_turn instead of reporting the tool result and completing the task.

fault location.explanation: The FunctionToolResultEvent branch reads event.result before publishing the tool result.
The exception handler emits error text, then returns the ordinary end_turn stop reason.

Root cause: SOURCE LOCATION CONFIRMED AT THE TESTED COMMIT; BEHAVIOR SUPPORTED BY THE ARCHIVED CANDIDATE REPORT. The ACP tool-stream handler reads event.result, whereas the recorded pydantic-ai-slim 2.59.0 result event exposes part. The write side effect has already happened when attribute access fails. The exception handler sends Error text and the method returns end_turn; the requested done response and subsequent agent processing are lost. The original report labels this a defect candidate pending human review. It records 11 attempts (10 original plus one replacement): 10 valid executions and one Docker/infrastructure failure, original batch run-08, with no ACP/network trace found there. The old strict predicate counted 9/10 valid runs; the remaining valid run also showed the crash and file creation but lacked a tool_call start event after initial model text. This event-visibility difference is not evidence that the fault disappeared. This case and #249 use the same underlying executions and must not be counted as independent batches. Reproduction prerequisites: use the documented Custom Agent Factory, with the same build_agent as apps/acp/__main__.py and a models entry whose value is openai-chat:deepseek-chat; use an empty workspace and send the two steps as separate turns in one ACP session. This bypasses the separate stock-entry model-selection defect (#250) without changing the faulty prompt handler. Retain ACP stderr/error events, network logs and file evidence; lack of a tool_call event alone does not establish that no tool executed. Source and issue were checked for this file, but no new ACP/model run, dependency-wheel inspection or patch regression was performed. Dependency facts and reproduction counts are attributed to the archive; no claim is made about every allowed dependency version or the current default branch. No fixing revision/release was established. Tested source provenance: archived pydantic-deep 0.3.50 workspace at 650b592b6accd7dc994226abbaa0cf717527e457. The archive records pydantic-ai-slim 2.59.0, pydantic-ai-backend 0.2.37, pydantic-ai-harness 0.59.0, agent-client-protocol 0.12.1 and openai 3.35.1; dependencies were resolved without a lockfile. Reproducing only the repository commit does not guarantee the same dependency environment. pinned_contains_fix=false refers to this historical tested commit, not the current upstream default branch. Issue state was checked on 2026-10-26.
